threats.title: Stored name readable by other apps or from device backups
threats.description: The last entered name is a personal identifier kept in the Keychain. If the item is saved with a permissive accessibility class (such as kSecAttrAccessibleAlways) or with iCloud sync enabled, it can be read on a locked or compromised device, or from backups. A shared keychain access group could also expose it to other apps.

mitigations.text: Store the item with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly, no kSecAttrSynchronizable, and no shared access group.
Use the Keychain for persistent storage only. Do not copy the name to UserDefaults, files or logs.

threats.title: Unvalidated name written to the Keychain
threats.description: The entered name is stored without length or content limits. Oversized or malformed input could corrupt the stored item or fill the store. Saves are also not tied to a specific query, so a save could overwrite an unrelated item.

mitigations.text: Validate and trim the name (maximum length, allowed characters) before saving. Use a fixed service and account key with SecItemUpdate or SecItemAdd, and check the returned OSStatus.

threats.title: Loaded Keychain value trusted without validation
threats.description: A value read back from the Keychain could have been altered on a jailbroken device or by another process. If the app uses it without validation or decodes it unsafely, it could be displayed or processed in a harmful way.

mitigations.text: Treat the loaded value as untrusted. Decode it as UTF-8 with a length limit, fall back to an empty state on failure, and render it only as plain text.

threats.title: Name exposed through logs, screenshots or the app switcher
threats.description: The greeting and last name are shown on screen. They can be written to system logs, captured in app-switcher snapshots, or exposed to the pasteboard or keyboard cache. Other parties on the device could then read them.

mitigations.text: Do not log the name. Use os_log privacy markers (.private) if logging is needed.
Mark the input field as non-autocorrecting and hide or blur the content when the app moves to the background.

threats.title: Malicious or oversized input from the user
threats.description: The user can enter very long strings, control characters or format-string-like text. This may cause UI hangs, a crash or an unexpected greeting when the name is interpolated.

mitigations.text: Limit input length and strip control characters. Build the greeting with safe string interpolation and never use it as a format string.

threats.title: Crash or hang on Keychain failure or bad input
threats.description: The app may crash or block the main thread when a Keychain call fails (for example when the device is locked or an item is missing) or when it receives very large input. The user then cannot use the app.

mitigations.text: Handle every OSStatus error without force-unwrapping. Run Keychain calls off the main thread and show a safe default state on failure.

threats.title: No record of stored-name changes or Keychain errors
threats.description: The app does not log when the stored name is saved or cleared, or when Keychain operations fail. Failed or unexpected writes cannot be investigated afterwards. This is low risk for a single-user local app.

mitigations.text: Log Keychain operation outcomes (status codes only, with no name value) through the unified logging system.

threats.title: CI pipeline pinned to a mutable tag of the factory workflow
threats.description: The diff moves the reusable workflow reference and factory-ref from @main to @v1. A tag can be moved or retagged. Anyone who gains control of the upstream repository could run code in this repository's workflow, which has write permissions and `secrets: inherit`. That code could tamper with the app build or leak secrets.

mitigations.text: Pin the reusable workflow and factory-ref to a full commit SHA, and keep the workflow permissions minimal. Pass only the secrets the workflow needs instead of `secrets: inherit`.

threats.title: Substituted Keychain item on a compromised device
threats.description: On a jailbroken device an attacker could replace or pre-seed the Keychain item. The app would then show an attacker-chosen name as the last user. Without a Secure Enclave-backed access control the app cannot tell the value was not written by itself.

mitigations.text: Set an access control on the item and treat the stored value as non-authoritative display data. Optionally detect jailbreak and warn the user.
